comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C28-C34, C65-C66. Both evaluations find the capacitance measurement evidence for endocytic blockade compelling and supported. OpenEval provides detailed technical validation while peer reviewers affirm the case for fast endocytosis in site clearance.

Complete agreement on claims C8, C42-C43. Both accept the finding that endocytic blockers do not prolong STD recovery under physiological conditions, despite contrast with prior literature. OpenEval notes the mechanistic explanation is incomplete; peer reviewers accept without critique.

Full agreement on claims C4, C53-C57. Both evaluations support the finding that endocytic blockers reduce facilitation at hippocampal synapses. OpenEval notes the unexplained Dynasore-specific basal amplitude effect warrants caution; peer reviewers accept without raising this concern.

Complete agreement on claims C81-C83, C87-C88. Both accept findings about calcium concentration effects and Latrunculin equipotency. OpenEval notes C88 is somewhat speculative; peer reviewers implicitly accept by emphasizing physiologically optimized conditions.

Strong agreement on claims C5, C46-C49, C75-C76 regarding scaffold inhibitor effects. Both highlight this as a key finding showing frequency-dependent enhancement of STD independent of endocytosis. OpenEval includes C83 in analysis; peer reviewers focus on the core scaffold findings.

Agreement on claims C50-C52 regarding co-application experiments. Both support the complementary mechanism model. OpenEval notes the mechanistic interpretation is somewhat speculative; peer reviewers affirm the interpretation of synapse-specific differences without expressing reservations.

Strong agreement on claims C6, C58, C77 showing differential effects across synapse types. Both highlight this as a key finding. OpenEval includes C78; peer reviewers emphasize this as 'the most interesting finding' regarding synapse-specific scaffold mechanisms.

Agreement on claims C67-C71 regarding quantitative analysis linking endocytic rates to EPSC changes. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to reliance on unpublished data (C68) and approximate nature of estimates; peer reviewers SUPPORT without challenging the analysis, implicitly accepting the quantitative case.

Substantial agreement on frequency-dependent synaptic depression enhancement. OpenEval covers C3, C35-C41, C61-C64, C70-C71 with detailed kinetic analysis; peer reviewers focus on C3, C7, C35-C38, C40, C61-C62, C64. Both support the presynaptic mechanism and frequency-dependent nature.

Agreement on main conclusions C9-C10 (OpenEval) and C9, C78 (peer). Both support the universal role of endocytic site clearance and synapse-specific scaffold mechanisms. OpenEval notes 'universal' may be overstated with only two synapse types; peer reviewers accept the comprehensive comparative nature.

Partial overlap on presynaptic mechanism claims C39-C41. OpenEval includes these in broader frequency-dependent analysis (R2); peer reviewers separately evaluate presynaptic interpretation. Both support the presynaptic locus without postsynaptic contributions.

Partial overlap on C74 regarding slow endocytosis function. OpenEval rates C74 as UNCERTAIN speculation about preventing membrane accumulation; peer reviewers group with C72-C73 and SUPPORT the distinction between fast and slow endocytosis roles without challenging the housekeeping interpretation.

Partial overlap on C60 regarding Bafilomycin/Folimycin effects. OpenEval rates R11 (C60, C89-C90) as UNCERTAIN due to highly speculative C90 about LTP/memory; peer reviewers focus on C60, C93 and SUPPORT as appropriately cautious negative findings.

Partial overlap on C93 regarding UFE physiological role. OpenEval evaluates C91-C93 as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable conclusion that UFE role is unclear; peer reviewers group C60, C93 together and accept as appropriately cautious about mechanisms not clearly demonstrated.
